data.title: Rate hike on the cards? Markets say increasingly likely
data.description:
The odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month have jumped sharply, with markets increasingly signaling that policymakers could raise rates at their September meeting following the latest inflation data.

The CME FedWatch data showed an 85.4% probability of a hike to 375-400 basis points, up from 72.4% a day earlier and 59.4% a week earlier. The probability of the Fed holding its current 350-375-basis-point target range fell to 14.6%, from 27.6% a day earlier and 40.6% a week earlier.

The repricing came after August headline CPI rose 0.4% month over month, matching expectations, while core CPI increased 0.3%, slightly above the 0.2% consensus.

The Fed is scheduled to meet on Sept. 15-16.

A separate chart shared by Kevin Gordon, Head of Macro Research and Strategy, Schwab Center for Financial Research, showed market pricing for a September hike had risen to 88%, reinforcing the sharp move in expectations following the inflation report.

data.title: Bread Financial initiated with Hold equivalent at Wells Fargo
data.description:
Wells Fargo initiated coverage of Bread Financial Holdings (BFH) with Equal Weight rating and a $115.00 price target.

Shares were 0.63% lower at $106.19 during morning trading on Friday.

"Reflecting balance sheet and credit improvement, the stock has significantly outperformed card-issuing peers over the past year. We see continued positive momentum on credit metrics as they migrate back to historical net charge-off levels," said analyst Donald Fandetti.

"Thus far, higher gas prices/inflation have not affected card spend or delinquency rates. We view '26 guidance line items as reasonable, with potential for slight improvement in H2," said Fandetti.

Wells Fargo's rating differs from Seeking Alpha authors as well as sell-side analysts rating of Buy. SA's Quant Rating system grades the stock as Strong Buy.

data.title: Colgate-Palmolive evaluating sale of some personal care brands - Reuters
data.description:
Colgate-Palmolive (CL) is considering a sale of certain mass-market personal care ‌brands, including Softsoap, Irish Spring and Speed Stick.

The consumer goods company is working with Goldman Sachs on a sales process, according to a  Reuters report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. Colgate (CL) only plans to divest a few brands in its personal care unit that could see more than $1 billion in a sale.

Colgate and ​Goldman Sachs declined to comment to Reuters.

Shares of Colgate (CL) ticked lower by 0.1% on Friday.

data.title: 66 months later, U.S. inflation still won't hit 2%
data.description:
Headline inflation remained above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target for a 66th consecutive month in August, underscoring how far price pressures remain from the central bank’s goal.

Headline CPI rose 0.4% month over month, matching forecasts. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3%, a slight tick above the 0.2% consensus.

The chart posted by Charlie Bilello, chief market strategist at Creative Planning, showed inflation rising from 2.6% in March 2021 to a peak of 9% in June 2022 before falling sharply, reaching 3% in May 2023 and a low of about 2.3% in March 2025.

Inflation then moved higher again, reaching 4.2% in May 2026 before easing to 3.5% in June and 3.4% in both July and August, the chart showed.

Bilello said the prolonged period of inflation above the Fed’s target showed that the central bank had “lost all credibility” when it came to fighting inflation.

data.title: 'Blasé markets' are ignoring record diesel prices, BofA warns
data.description:
While $100-a-barrel crude oil (USO) (BNO) is grabbing the headlines, Bank of America Securities is warning that a record-breaking surge in diesel prices is the true threat to the real economy, creating a dangerous recipe for market volatility.

Diesel prices surged above $6 a gallon for the first time on record, raising concerns about renewed energy-driven inflation just ahead of the fuel’s peak-demand season. The August Consumer Price Index report out earlier Friday showed Americans felt the burn at the pump as surging energy costs from the Middle East conflict continued to drive inflation, although that didn't seem to bother equities as major indices gapped up around 1% each at the time of writing.

Investors and policymakers are showing "no panic anywhere," even as the 30-year yield (US30Y) hits its highest level since June 2007 amid broadly spiking commodities, BofA analysts wrote in a recent note, arguing that this combination of "blasé markets" and "bravado policy" is masking severe underlying pressures.

BofA emphasized that diesel fuel serves as the central pressure point for critical real-economy sectors, including shipping, trucking, agriculture, construction and mining. Although crude oil prices remain markedly below their Ukraine-era peaks, U.S. average diesel prices have spiked to a record. This aggressive climb has also resulted in a widening gap between the national average costs of diesel and regular unleaded gasoline.

data.title: U.S. growth holds up as inflation, inequality pressure households
data.description:
The U.S. economy remains resilient, but the gains are increasingly uneven as growth holds up while the center of the economy hollows out, according to Diane Swonk, Chief Economist and Managing Director at KPMG LLP.

Swonk said real GDP is forecast to grow about 2% in 2026, matching last year’s pace, before cooling only modestly in 2027. However, the headline growth figures mask significant disparities across the economy.

Consumer spending remains relatively strong, supported by state and local tax cuts, stronger hiring and spending by affluent households, while lower- and middle-income consumers have become more cautious.

Housing, meanwhile, has been in recession for roughly two years as elevated financing and construction costs weigh on activity, while business investment remains heavily dominated by AI and data center construction.

The divide is also visible in consumer sentiment, Swonk said. Spending has held up even as confidence weakened further in August, with inflation, gasoline prices and job security among the key concerns.

She pointed to growing income and wealth inequality, noting that the top 1% of earners now owns more than half of U.S. equities and mutual funds, while the bottom half owns close to 1%.

Swonk said the concentration of economic gains at the top is reducing the financial cushion available to lower- and middle-income households and contributing to weaker trust in institutions and greater political polarization.

Inflation is another major challenge, with Swonk expecting the personal consumption expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, to remain above the central bank’s 2% target until late 2028.

She cited sticky services inflation, broad-based price increases, tariffs, weather disruptions and elevated energy and transportation costs as factors likely to keep inflation elevated.

Geopolitical tensions, including the Middle East conflict and trade frictions with Canada, could add further supply-chain pressures, while AI investment, defense spending and wider fiscal deficits are increasing competition for capital.

Swonk expects the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by another 50 basis points before the end of the year, arguing that delaying action could require more aggressive tightening later.

She also expects the 10-year Treasury yield to cross 5% and remain elevated for an extended period as persistent inflation, larger government borrowing, rising AI-related capital needs and weaker foreign demand for U.S. debt put upward pressure on long-term rates.

Swonk said the central economic challenge is no longer simply maintaining growth, but ensuring that its benefits reach more households rather than becoming increasingly concentrated at the top.

data.title: Adobe's earnings show ARR growth deceleration amid freemium strategy: analysts
data.description:
Adobe (ADBE) shares declined less than 1% during early Friday action following its third-quarter results as analysts noted a slowdown in growth to annual recurring revenue as the creative software provider pursues its freemium AI strategy.

"Adobe reported muted 3Q results with ARR growth continuing to slow and sequential declines in RPO/cRPO as the company continues to navigate meaningful pressure in its Creative business," according to Citi analysts in a Friday investor note. "Calculated NNARR of $400M missed our estimate by ~10% and implies a staggering 39% Y/Y decline. With unchanged annual ARR guidance of 10.2%, Q4 setup looks more aggressive, barring an improvement in other demand or seasonality factors. While we look to get more clarity under the strategy of recently appointed CEO Anil Chakravarthy and a potential CFO hire, we believe shares are likely to be range-bound amidst decelerating growth."

Citi retained its Neutral rating but reduced its price target to $250 from $301.

Meanwhile, Morgan Stanley maintained its Underweight rating and $240 target.

"The quarter offered stronger adoption signals and solid near-term execution but limited incremental evidence of a financial inflection to serve as a positive catalyst," said Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Wood in a note. "Revenue grew 13% YoY / 12% YoY CC and was ~1% above guidance (slightly below the ~2%-2.5% beats in 1H), while total ARR reached $27.5B, with ~$400M of net new ARR ahead of expectations, though down 38% YoY as Adobe continues to route more demand through freemium experiences ahead of paid conversion."

Jefferies kept its Hold rating but nudged its price target down to $275 from $285.

"AI metrics continue to move forward, with direct ARR up ~30% q/q to >$650M, though still representing only ~2% of total ARR," said Jefferies analyst Brent Thill.

Finally, J.P. Morgan was the most upbeat on the stock, reiterating its Overweight rating while lowering its price target to $315 from $340.

"We are tweaking our revenue and earnings estimates following the results, and despite a forecasted deceleration in revenue growth in FY27, we believe the inexpensive 8x 2027 uFCF multiple presents a low bar for upsides to the share price from a recovery in monetization as new customers progress through the freemium funnel over time to support more robust monetization for the company," said J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee in a note.

data.title: Laser weapons, space dogfights, and humanoid robots: The future of the battlefield
data.description:
New frontiers are emerging on the battlefield, with countries increasingly investing in laser weapons, space warfare and even humanoid robots.

Once a staple of science fiction, laser weapons are now a military reality for the U.S.

For instance, the U.S. used a high-energy laser weapon system for the first time to down suspicious drones near the Mexico border. The U.S. Air Forces in Europe and Air Forces Africa have used Boeing's (BA) Compact Laser Weapon System to combat drones overseas.

This month, the U.S. Army awarded its first production contract for high-energy laser weapon systems to AeroVironment (AVAV). Lockheed Martin (LMT) and nLight secured contracts for the Joint Laser Weapon System, which will be capable of downing drones and cruise missiles.

"High-energy lasers and high-power microwaves are becoming essential elements of naval warfare," Daryl Caudle, Chief of Naval Operations, wrote in a recent memo. "The question is no longer whether these systems work – it is how quickly we can field them across the fleet."

Elsewhere, Rafael Advanced Defense Systems delivered the Iron Beam to the Israel Defense Forces last year – the world's first combat deployment of a high-power laser-based aerial interception system.

Space warfare is now a strategic focus for countries. "Space is increasingly viewed as a critical operating domain, underpinning communications, navigation, and full-spectrum combat capabilities – with the next peer-to-peer conflict involving the U.S. and its allies likely to extend into space," Goldman Sachs analysts observed recently.

President Trump's Golden Dome program envisions one space-based layer that includes sensors and intercept capabilities, as well as three land-based layers. The Pentagon is targeting to conduct the Golden Dome's first major test in H2 2028.

This week, the U.S. Space Command practiced "orbital dogfighting" – maneuvering satellites in proximity to one another in a simulated conflict environment. Chinese satellites reportedly demonstrated this capability in 2024.

The Space Force has forecast the U.S. satellite fleet growing from about 7K in 2025 to ~30K in 2040, while China's fleet is seen expanding from 1.9K in 2025 to ~21K in 2040. To maintain its edge, the agency called for deepening partnerships with commercial space companies.

Meanwhile, robotics have been grabbing headlines, with China touting its advances at the recent World Humanoid Robot Games.

Now Beijing is ramping up research into humanoids' military uses and planning for their eventual deployment in the battlefield, Reuters reported, citing government records. To note, there is no evidence that China deployed an armed humanoid with an operational military unit.

The U.S. military is also testing humanoid robots, but this is limited to handling weapons and not firing them. The Army also has an ongoing contest for humanoid technology with militarized capabilities. 

For now, humanoid robots still have a long way to go before they can be deployed in the battlefield. Sam Bresnick, research fellow at Georgetown University Center for Security and Emerging Technology, believes it could take 5-10 years.

Related stocks: AeroVironment (AVAV), Lockheed Martin (LMT), RTX (RTX), Kratos (KTOS), Northrop Grumman (NOC), Boeing (BA), SpaceX (SPCX), Rocket Lab (RKLB), L3Harris (LHX), Viasat (VSAT).

Humanoid robot makers: Tesla (TSLA), Hyundai (HYMLF)-owned Boston Dynamics, Nvidia (NVDA)-backed Figure AI, XPeng (XPEV), China's Unitree.

data.title: Robinhood's August data offers investors a reason to stay
data.description:
Robinhood Markets (HOOD) shares were trading at $112.81 at the time of writing after a weekly decline of nearly 10%.

Still, the stock has gained 25.45% from Aug. 1 to date, sharply outperforming the S&P 500 (SP500), which returned -0.11% over the same period.

The latest August operating data helps explain why investors continue to watch the brokerage closely.

“Platform growth remains the key story.”

Robinhood officially stated that it ended the month with 28.6M funded customers, up about 120K from July and 1.90M from a year earlier. Total platform assets climbed 8% M/M to $383.7B, while net deposits reached $4.0B.

Trading activity was also strong in traditional markets. Equity trading volume rose 68% YoY to $335.4B, while options contracts increased 50% to 292.5M.

Event contracts also continued their explosive expansion, reaching 4.7B, up roughly 15x YoY.

Crypto was the biggest monthly rebound. Crypto trading volume jumped 61% from July to $17.5B, although it remained 38% below August 2025 levels.

Robinhood’s app crypto volume rose 72% M/M to $7.4B, while Bitstamp volume increased 53% to $10.1B.

Meanwhile, margin balances climbed 72% YoY to $21.5B, pointing to stronger interest income potential.

The bigger investor question is no longer whether Robinhood can grow but how much of that growth can translate into durable earnings.

With the stock now pulling back after a powerful run, August’s numbers give investors a reason to look beyond the weekly weakness. Still, the elevated valuation means continued operating growth will need to keep matching expectations.

data.title: SFL extends charter for six container vessels with Hapag-Lloyd, adding $750M to backlog
data.description:
SFL Corp. (SFL) gained 2.4% in early trading Friday after saying it agreed to a seven-year charter extension for six 15,400 TEU container vessels with Hapag-Lloyd (HPGLY) (HLAGF), in an indication of the strength of the current container ship charter market.

The new time charter contracts will provide charter coverage for the vessels until 2035-36 at firm rates and add ~$750M to SFL's (SFL) fixed-rate charter backlog, increasing the backlog to ~$4.6B.

"We have added more than $1B to our charter backlog during 2026, underpinning our strong earnings visibility and supporting a long-term distribution capacity going forward," SFL Management (SFL) CEO Ole Hjertaker said.
